key_insight: LoRA’s learning complexity depends on which low-rank updates the pretrained network can statistically distinguish, not simply on its trainable parameter count.
engineering_relevance: Layer-specific activation and gradient geometry can help assess LoRA’s effective complexity beyond adapter rank or parameter budget.
method: Locally linearize LoRA as low-rank trace regression with a forward-backward covariance.
Analyze singular geometry using observable tangent directions and affine sections of determinantal varieties.
Estimate the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) with a curvature-corrected multi-temperature estimator.
evidence_signal: Experiments on multilayer perceptrons and transformers show strongly layer-dependent geometry; ambient covariance degeneracy does not necessarily imply degeneracy along relevant low-rank directions.
watch_item: The local linearization is an approximation, and global learning complexity can be dominated by singularities away from the ground-truth rank stratum.
